open_obligations.what_is_open: The compact-window second-order risk approximation and sequential coercivity for bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), and \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact risk identity contains only the deletion and action-loss components, but the frozen primitives do not control either component uniformly at the \(n^{-3/2}\) scale. The first-order oracle-gain theorem supplies only an \(o(n^{-1})\) remainder, the pilot-information audit prevents replacing the realized pilot information by \(I(\beta)\), and the unresolved finite-boundary comparison is needed to rule out second-order tie and unequal-inclusion corrections.
open_obligations.attempted: Reused the exact two-component identity, the first-order oracle-gain expansion, first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule, both proved macroscopic exclusions, and the conditional deterministic balanced-grid transfer. These results isolate but do not prove the finite-boundary and information-to-action comparisons required at frontier scale.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact identity
\[
R_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)-R_n^{\mathrm{or}}(\beta)
=D_{n,m}(\beta)+L_{n,m}(\delta_m,\beta)
\]
and the conditional deterministic balanced-grid transfer are proved.  Uniformly for \(m/\sqrt n\) in compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\), the missing compact-window premise reduces to the coefficient-level comparisons
\[
D_{n,m}(\beta)
=A(\beta)\frac{m}{n^2}+o(n^{-3/2}),
\qquad
L_{n,m}(\widehat G_m,\beta)
=\frac{B(\beta)}{nm}+o(n^{-3/2}),
\]
together with the matching arbitrary-rule lower comparison.  The two branches of \(\mathrm{lem{:}pilot\text{-}endpoint\text{-}exclusion}\) prove coercivity when \(N=o(n)\) and when both waves retain nonvanishing fractions.  The only unresolved boundary regimes are bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), and \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\).  Neither coefficient-level expansion follows from the proved first-order oracle gain.

prose_updates.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-\(\alpha\) main-wave mixture retain exact Horvitz--Thompson centering for the realized finite-population factorial vector. The proved contribution includes the exact two-component risk identity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain limit, and first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule. The two proved branches rule out a fixed nondegenerate wave split and a sublinear main wave. The deterministic balanced-grid result remains conditional: compact-window second-order convergence, the pilot-information bridge, and three boundary regimes remain open, so no square-root pilot recommendation is yet certified.

project_justification.gap: Existing factorial rerandomization theory supplies first-order Gaussian precision and existing two-wave work supplies accounting architecture, but neither proves the moving-boundary exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison at the square-root pilot scale. The present information audit also shows that the stated moment conditions do not identify the pilot Fisher-information limit.
project_justification.niche: On a fixed complete baseline array with a full-dimensional product parameter domain, the design problem separates exactly into a deletion contrast and a potentially signed action-loss contrast. A compactness, leave-one-unit, and Gaussian lower-tail argument controls the latter at first order for every admissible finite-score rule, while the uniform deletion identity handles nonconvergent pilot fractions whenever the main wave diverges.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact pooled Horvitz--Thompson accounting, the explicit first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient, first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule, both macroscopic exclusion branches, the exact pilot likelihood and realized-information audit, and a conditional deterministic grid-transfer certificate. It leaves both frontier coefficients, compact-window convergence, the information-to-action bridge, and the three remaining boundary comparisons as explicit open questions.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Discrete score supports can create exact ties, and induced designs can have unequal inclusion probabilities. Compact rule and parameter subsequences, zero Gaussian boundary mass, an explicit leave-one-unit coupling, and exact residual cancellation absorb those effects only at first order. They do not provide an \(n^{-3/2}\) remainder, so they do not establish the compact-window second-order premise or the three remaining boundary comparisons. Separately, smooth first and second outcome moments do not control score information as a function of the baseline, so the pilot LAN information cannot be fixed at \(I(\beta)\) without additional derivation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson centering and accounting, the one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, first-order Gaussian lower-tail optimality against every admissible finite-score rule, the exact pilot likelihood and information audit, the two proved macroscopic exclusions covering fixed nondegenerate wave splits and sublinear main waves, and the conditional deterministic grid transfer. The coefficient \(A\) remains an unresolved deletion candidate and \(B\) remains a Gaussian action candidate. Uniform frontier-scale deletion, exact finite action curvature, information convergence, bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), the regime \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\), and the unconditional global pilot rule are open. The causal estimand remains the fixed realized factorial vector throughout.
